p: numbered the people that were with: For certain of the Reubenites, Gadites, and of the half tribe could not bear the insolence of the son against the father, and therefore joined with David.
now thou art worth ten thousand: Signifying that a good governor is so dear to his people that they would rather lose their lives than have anything happen to him.
wood of Ephraim: So called, because the Ephraimites (as some say) fed their cattle beyond Jordan in this wood.
blew the trumpet: For he had pity on the people, who were seduced by Absalom's flattery.
pit in the wood: Thus God turned his vain glory to shame.
son to keep my name in: It seemed that God had punished him by taking away his children, 2Sa 14:27.
shalt not bear tidings this day: For Joab bore a good affection to Ahimaaz and doubted how David would take the report of Absalom's death.
gates: He sat in the gate of the city of Mahanaim.
good man: He had experienced his fidelity, 2Sa 17:21.
servant: That is, Cushi, who was an Ethiopian.
moved: Because he considers both the judgment of God against his sin, and could not otherwise hide his fatherly affection for his son.
